1	# Runtime Checklist
2	
3	## Binary Selection
4	
5	- Prefer an installed `unity-cli` binary when it exists on `PATH` (the installer links it to `~/.local/bin/unity-cli`).
6	- If no binary is installed, run `scripts/install.sh` (macOS / Linux) or `scripts/install.ps1` (Windows, when published) instead of asking the user.
7	- Only inside a unity-cli source checkout, `cargo run -- <args>` is a development alternative.
8	
9	## Project Setup
10	
11	- `unity-cli setup` = binary check → `bridge install` → Editor `ping`; it prints one JSON report and exits non-zero until the Editor answers for this project.
12	- Tell the user before running it: it edits `Packages/manifest.json` and, when the project uses only the legacy Input Manager and the Editor is closed, sets `activeInputHandler: 2` (Both) in `ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset` so the Input System dependency does not block the Editor with a restart dialog. `bridge install` is idempotent (a second run leaves both files byte-identical).
13	- If the Editor was already open, it may show "enable the Input System backends? (restart)"; bridge commands time out until someone answers it. Close the Editor and rerun `setup --launch-editor` instead.
14	- `--launch-editor` starts the Unity Hub Editor recorded in `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt` (`UNITY_EDITOR_PATH` overrides) and waits up to 900 s (`--wait-secs`).
15	- `editor.projectMatches: false` means another project's Editor owns the port; pass `--port`.
16	- `versionCheck.status: mismatch` (from `setup` or `system ping`) → `unity-cli bridge upgrade`, or update the CLI.
17	- Verify the binary with `unity-cli --version` before debugging higher-level workflows.
18	
19	## Instance Selection
20	
21	- Use `unity-cli system ping` when a single active target is expected.
22	- Use `unity-cli instances list` when multiple editors may be running.
23	- Prefer `--project-path <project>` (or running inside the project) to target one Editor; `AMBIGUOUS_EDITOR` lists candidates in `data.candidates`.
24	- Use `unity-cli instances set-active <host:port>` only after confirming the target is `up`.
25	
26	## Command Routing
27	
28	- The bootstrap-relevant typed subcommands are `system ping`, `scene create`, `instances list`, `instances set-active`. Use them when available. (`instances list` / `instances set-active` are local registry operations rather than bridge-tool wrappers.)
29	- The `reference *` family (`fetch`, `status`, `search`, `grep`, `view`, `find-symbol`, `diff`, `resolve-symbol-at`, `embed-build`, `embed-search`, `clean`) also has typed wrappers over the `reference_*` bridge tools — see the `unity-csharp-reference` skill. Beyond these, most bridge tools have no typed wrapper.
30	- For every tool without a typed wrapper, use `unity-cli raw <tool_name> --json '{...}'` (or its alias `unity-cli tool call <tool_name> --json '{...}'`). This is the primary invocation pattern, not a fallback — bridge tools such as `analyze_scene_contents`, `find_by_component`, `modify_component`, and `get_compilation_state` are all invoked this way.
31	- Discover tools with `unity-cli tool list --query <term> --compact`; add `--category <name>` (a `docs/tools.md` heading or slug such as `scenes`, `playback-testing`) and `--limit N` / `--offset N` to keep output small. Inspect a tool's expected JSON payload with `unity-cli tool schema <tool_name> --output json`.
32	- Use `--output json` when another tool or script will consume the result.
33	
34	## Connection Recovery
35	
36	- A failed `system ping` does not prove the Editor is closed. Run `unity-cli doctor --output json` (add `--project-path <dir>` outside the project) before any fallback such as hand-editing YAML.
37	- Act on the `diagnosis` code:
38	  - `SAFE_MODE` / `COMPILE_ERRORS`: the bridge is not loaded. Fix each `editorLog.compileErrors[]` entry (`file`, `line`, `code`) by editing the file directly, then let Unity recompile or restart the Editor.
39	  - `BRIDGE_NOT_INSTALLED`: run `unity-cli setup` (or `unity-cli bridge install`) to add `com.akiojin.unity-cli-bridge` to `Packages/manifest.json`.
40	  - `PORT_IN_USE`: `port.listenerPid` / `port.listenerProcess` hold the port. Stop it or change the bridge port and pass the same `--port`.
41	  - `EDITOR_NOT_RUNNING`: start the Editor for the project and wait for import to finish.
42	  - `SANDBOX_BLOCKED`: the local socket was denied. Retry in a permitted execution context according to the host's approval policy; do not bypass sandbox restrictions or conclude the Editor is missing. If reachability still cannot be verified, ask the user to confirm the running project and bridge connection before considering an offline fallback.
43	  - `BRIDGE_NOT_RESPONDING`: the Editor is still importing/compiling or the port differs from Project Settings > Unity CLI Bridge.
44	- Re-run `unity-cli doctor` until `diagnosis` is `OK`, then continue the workflow.
45	- An empty instance list or failed process probe inside a sandbox is also inconclusive. Confirm the project/host/port and the user's Editor state instead of treating restricted visibility as `EDITOR_NOT_RUNNING`.
46	- When the target Editor is reachable, never hand-edit serialized `.unity`, `.prefab`, or `.asset` YAML. Bridge operations keep serialized references, prefab overrides, and the live Editor state in sync.
47	- If recovery cannot restore the connection and offline work is appropriate, declare the fallback before editing: explain the verified limitation, affected files, alternative method, and how the result will be checked after reopening Unity. Without confirmation of an uncertain sandbox diagnosis, pause dependent edits. Do not silently substitute YAML edits for bridge calls.
48	
49	## CI Notes
50	
51	- Set `UNITY_CLI_HOST` and `UNITY_CLI_PORT` explicitly in CI.
52	- Keep JSON payloads quoted as a single shell argument.
53	- If connectivity fails in CI, report the resolved host and port before retrying.
54

1	# Localization construction and verification
2	
3	Use public APIs from the installed package, through `unity-cli editor eval`.
4	Keep calls synchronous and short; query async completion in subsequent calls.
5	Inspect `unity-cli tool schema eval_csharp` and `get_ui_element_state` before
6	constructing payloads. A transport success containing a tool error is failure.
7	
8	## Package and assets
9	
10	Inspect package metadata before choosing a version. Unity 2022.3 publishes
11	Localization 1.4.4; do not assume a Unity 6 package works on an older Editor.
12	Use `package_manager install`, then wait for ping, `isCompiling:false`,
13	`isUpdating:false`, resolved package version and console checks.
14	
15	Choose a scoped folder, such as `Assets/Localization/Demo`. In repository E2E,
16	use `Assets/Scenes/Generated/E2E/Localization` for generated scenes/assets.
17	Inspect existing settings before creating any asset. Use
18	`LocalizationEditorSettings.ActiveLocalizationSettings` to select an existing
19	settings asset, or persist a new `LocalizationSettings` asset and assign it.
20	Do not replace an existing project's startup selectors or Addressables groups.
21	
22	For each requested code, use `Locale.CreateLocale("en")` / `("ja")` only when
23	that locale is absent, save it with `AssetDatabase.CreateAsset`, then register
24	it with `LocalizationEditorSettings.AddLocale`. Verify both are available.
25	
26	Use `LocalizationEditorSettings.GetStringTableCollection(name)` to detect an
27	existing collection. Otherwise call `CreateStringTableCollection(name, folder,
28	locales)`. This handles shared data and Addressables registration; creating loose
29	`StringTable` objects does not establish the complete collection. Use
30	`collection.GetTable(locale.Identifier)`, add a missing locale table when needed,
31	and call `StringTable.AddEntry(key, translation)`. Mark changed tables and
32	`SharedData` dirty, then `AssetDatabase.SaveAssets`. Read back matching shared key
33	IDs and each exact translation. Example values: key `greeting`, English
34	`Hello, world!`, Japanese `こんにちは、世界！`.
35	
36	## Persistent UI binding
37	
38	Use the requested UGUI Text or TextMeshPro label. Assign its compatible font
39	asset with Japanese glyph coverage before judging the translation. A correct
40	`text` property with square replacement glyphs is not a successful visual check.
41	
42	Add/reuse `UnityEngine.Localization.Components.LocalizeStringEvent`. Configure
43	`StringReference.TableReference` and `TableEntryReference` with the persisted
44	collection and key. Wire its `OnUpdateString` to the text property setter using
45	`UnityEditor.Events.UnityEventTools.AddPersistentListener<string>` and a
46	`UnityEngine.Events.UnityAction<string>` targeting that setter. A temporary
47	`AddListener` lambda disappears on scene reload. Do not remove other listeners
48	or add a duplicate when retrying. Mark the component/scene dirty and save.
49	
50	Reload the scene in Edit Mode. Read the persistent event target/method, table
51	and key, and saved translations before entering Play. Do not replace a dirty
52	user scene without preserving its changes.
53	
54	## Runtime proof
55	
56	1. Enter Play. Wait for initialization completion and successful operation status;
57	   if it fails, inspect missing settings, locales and Addressables diagnostics.
58	   Do not block the main thread with a sleep or an async wait inside eval.
59	2. Set `LocalizationSettings.SelectedLocale` using
60	   `AvailableLocales.GetLocale("en")`; fail if it returns null.
61	3. Poll `get_ui_element_state` for the specific label until its actual `text`
62	   equals `Hello, world!`. Use a bounded deadline and allow frames between polls.
63	4. Capture Game view with `osFallback:false`; inspect the returned image.
64	5. Set the selected locale to `ja`, wait for `こんにちは、世界！`, and capture
65	   with identical camera/resolution. Inspect that the text is visible and legible.
66	6. Switch back to `en` and verify the original label text. Read console errors,
67	   stop Play and verify the saved assets and persistent event again.
68	
69	Do not use direct text assignment, editor preview alone or a String Database
70	lookup as proof of the live binding. If a Game capture omits overlay UI, retain
71	that failure and consult the separate capture issue #422; use an existing
72	supported capture path only when it captures the actual Game UI. No synthesized
73	images or silent OS-window fallback. Persist image paths, label state, versions,
74	saved Locale/table assets and the tool transcript as evidence.
75	
76	## API references and authorship
77	
78	This workflow is independently authored from the repository tool contract and
79	Unity's public package APIs, without official unity-agent-plugin skill content.
80	
81	- [Localization Editor APIs](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.localization@1.4/api/UnityEditor.Localization.LocalizationEditorSettings.html)
82	- [Localize String Event](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.localization@1.4/api/UnityEngine.Localization.Components.LocalizeStringEvent.html)
83	- [Unity 2022.3 package compatibility](https://docs.unity3d.com/2022.3/Documentation/Manual/com.unity.localization.html)
84
